title: Tensor products of symmetric bimodules are symmetric
statement:
Let $\mathcal C$ be a braided monoidal category with coequalizers such that $X\otimes-$ and
$-\otimes X$ preserve colimits for every $X$, and let $A$ be a monoid object. For
$A$-$A$-bimodules $P$ and $Q$ with actions $\gamma_P,\rho_P,\gamma_Q,\rho_Q$, the tensor
product over $A$ is the coequalizer
$$
P\otimes_AQ=\operatorname{coeq}\bigl(P\otimes A\otimes Q\rightrightarrows P\otimes Q\bigr)
$$
of $\rho_P\otimes Q$ and $(P\otimes\gamma_Q)\alpha_{P,A,Q}$. Here $A$ acts on the left
through $P$ and on the right through $Q$. If $P$ and $Q$ are symmetric in the sense of
[lem-sfb-modobj-symmetric-bimodules], then so is $P\otimes_AQ$.

proof.text: Put $T=P\otimes_A Q$, and let $\pi:P\otimes Q\to T$ be its coequalizer projection. Write $\alpha_{U,V,W}:(U\otimes V)\otimes W\to U\otimes(V\otimes W)$, and read composites right to left. Since $-\otimes A$ preserves this coequalizer, $q=\pi\otimes A$ is the coequalizer projection of the two defining arrows tensored with $A$. By the universal property in [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit], applied to the parallel-pair diagram, write the tensored parallel arrows as $f,g:D\rightrightarrows (P\otimes Q)\otimes A$. The colimiting cocone has components $q$ and $qf=qg$. If $uq=vq$, then also $uqf=vqf$; hence $u$ and $v$ factor the same cocone on both objects, and uniqueness gives $u=v$. Thus $q$ is epi, and it suffices to prove $\rho_T q=\gamma_T\beta_{T,A}q$.

source.place: first paragraph; coequalizer cancellation expanded from its universal property

proof.text:
The induced actions in the statement satisfy
$$\rho_T(\pi\otimes A)=\pi(P\otimes\rho_Q)\alpha_{P,Q,A},\qquad
\gamma_T(A\otimes\pi)=\pi(\gamma_P\otimes Q)\alpha^{-1}_{A,P,Q}.$$
The definition of symmetric in [lem-sfb-modobj-symmetric-bimodules] gives $\rho_Q=\gamma_Q\beta_{Q,A}$ and $\rho_P=\gamma_P\beta_{P,A}$; only this definition is used, not the assertion about modules over a commutative monoid. The defining coequalizer relation is $\pi(P\otimes\gamma_Q)\alpha_{P,A,Q}=\pi(\rho_P\otimes Q)$. Substituting these equalities and using functoriality of tensor yields
$$\begin{aligned}
\rho_T q
&=\pi(P\otimes\gamma_Q)(P\otimes\beta_{Q,A})\alpha_{P,Q,A}\\
&=\pi(\rho_P\otimes Q)\alpha^{-1}_{P,A,Q}(P\otimes\beta_{Q,A})\alpha_{P,Q,A}\\
&=\pi(\gamma_P\otimes Q)(\beta_{P,A}\otimes Q)\alpha^{-1}_{P,A,Q}(P\otimes\beta_{Q,A})\alpha_{P,Q,A}.
\end{aligned}$$

source.place: second paragraph, substitutions and coequalizer relation

proof.text:
The reverse hexagon axiom for $P,Q,A$, with composites read right to left as in Step 1, is
$$\alpha^{-1}_{A,P,Q}\beta_{P\otimes Q,A}\alpha^{-1}_{P,Q,A}
=(\beta_{P,A}\otimes Q)\alpha^{-1}_{P,A,Q}(P\otimes\beta_{Q,A}).$$
Precomposing both sides with $\alpha_{P,Q,A}$ and cancelling $\alpha^{-1}_{P,Q,A}\alpha_{P,Q,A}$ gives
$$(\beta_{P,A}\otimes Q)\alpha^{-1}_{P,A,Q}(P\otimes\beta_{Q,A})\alpha_{P,Q,A}
=\alpha^{-1}_{A,P,Q}\beta_{P\otimes Q,A}.$$
Substitute this into Step 2. By the defining left-action equation there, and the naturality axiom $\beta_{T,A}(\pi\otimes A)=(A\otimes\pi)\beta_{P\otimes Q,A}$, the result is
$$\begin{aligned}
\rho_T q
&=\pi(\gamma_P\otimes Q)\alpha^{-1}_{A,P,Q}\beta_{P\otimes Q,A}\\
&=\gamma_T(A\otimes\pi)\beta_{P\otimes Q,A}\\
&=\gamma_T\beta_{T,A}q.
\end{aligned}$$
Cancellation by Step 1 proves $\rho_T=\gamma_T\beta_{T,A}$, the required symmetry equation. Only the hexagon and naturality axioms of the given braided category, not symmetry of its braiding, are used.

source.place: second paragraph, hexagon and braiding naturality
